faqs.q: What does the 24° Cone End Nut do and where is it used?
faqs.a: The 24° Cone End Nut is an end nut for a 24° cone fitting. It draws the cutting ring up the cone of the fitting body so the tube is held and sealed. It is listed in the Indus DIN 2353 Bite Type Adapters range with 20 part numbers, from M12×1.5 to M52×2.

faqs.a: IH-AD-DIN-004-L12 is the 24° Cone End Nut (listing code IH-AD-DIN-004) followed by a size suffix that the size table ties to the ends shown. In the table: IH-AD-DIN-004-L12 (suffix L12) is M12×1.5; IH-AD-DIN-004-S24 (suffix S24) is M24×1.5; IH-AD-DIN-004-S52 (suffix S52) is M52×2. Quote the full part number when you order.

faqs.q: Which sizes of 24° Cone End Nut do you list?
faqs.a: The 24° Cone End Nut is listed in 20 sizes, running from M12×1.5 to M52×2. The Sizes & Part Numbers tab gives the thread on each end for every part number, and sizes outside the table can be quoted on request.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right size of 24° Cone End Nut for my port?
faqs.a: Identify the thread type and the seat at each end first, then the size. For example, IH-AD-DIN-004-S24 is M24×1.5. A thread that engages against the wrong seat will weep under pressure, so confirm both before ordering. Our [checklist of what to send for a fittings quote](/blog/what-to-send-for-a-fittings-quote) shows what to measure.

faqs.q: Which standards does the 24° Cone End Nut follow?

faqs.q: What does the 24° Cone End Nut connect to?
faqs.a: The 24° Cone End Nut is used with a DIN 2353 24° cone fitting body and a tube of the size shown in the size table. The ring, the nut and the fitting body must all be the same series (light or heavy) and the same tube size. The [DIN 2353 Bite Type Adapters](/c/din-2353-bite-type-adapters-uae) range lists the bodies, nuts and rings.

faqs.q: How do I fit the 24° Cone End Nut so it does not leak?
faqs.a: Match the thread and the seat before you tighten the 24° Cone End Nut. On a 24° cone end the tube goes through the nut and cutting ring and is pre-set into the cone, so cut the tube square, deburr it and preset the ring before final assembly. Clean the port first and never force a joint that does not start by hand. See our [guide to diagnosing an over-tightened fitting](/blog/over-tightened-fitting-diagnosis) for more.
